[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the account lead, with Priya our solutions engineer and Maya from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Jamie Lawson: Doing well, thanks. Excited to get started, we've been looking forward to this.
[00:13] Maya Ortiz: Awesome. Quick agenda — go over timeline, requirements (network/SSO/KMS), pilot scope, and action items.
[00:22] Rita Gomez: Sounds good. We want to flag upfront — we have strict networking rules, and everything has to go through our VPC peering and use our KMS for key management.
[00:31] Priya Rao: Yep, that's totally supported. We offer Redwood Private with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; we also have Dedicated if you want reserved capacity. There's a few tradeoffs — dedicated gives predictable throughput but higher baseline cost.
[00:42] Dr. Isaac Park: For clinical workloads, latency variability is a concern. We need consistent sub-200ms p95 for short prompts, ideally. Does that sound doable?
[00:50] Priya Rao: For the prompt sizes you're describing, sub-200ms p95 is achievable on Dedicated in the region you're in. On hosted we can hit low latency too but you may see more variance. We'll run a benchmark to confirm with your sample traffic.
[01:05] Jamie Lawson: Our initial plan is a 6-week pilot covering triage and summarization flows. Success is measured by latency and a manual quality pass on 1k prompts. Also need to confirm data retention and logs for audit.
[01:20] Alex Chen: Got it. We'll make that pilot plan explicit. For audit logs we can provide per-request logging and export; we also have an option to keep logs for X days — we'll share the retention options.
[01:32] Rita Gomez: Also need SSO — SAML-based SSO and scoped RBAC. Can we hook into Okta?
[01:37] Maya Ortiz: Yes, Okta is in our standard SAML flow. We can set up SSO and map groups to roles. We'll send the SAML metadata and the setup steps.
[01:45] Jamie Lawson: Perfect. On the encryption side, KMS — we need to use our HSM-backed KMS. Is that supported?
[01:52] Priya Rao: We integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; for hosted we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) on enterprise plans. I'll include the KMS configuration guide.
[02:02] Alex Chen: Quick question on model variants — for cost reasons we may want to use a quantized variant for bulk embedding jobs and a higher-quality model for clinical summarization. Priya?
[02:12] Priya Rao: Yep, we can route by workload. The platform supports model variants and automatic fallback. We'll recommend quantization profiles per workload; Redwood Optimize will give suggestions based on your token mix.
[02:25] Dr. Isaac Park: On privacy, do you store prompts? We need confirmatory language for the DPA.
[02:31] Maya Ortiz: We'll send the DPA and the data handling policy. For private deployments data never leaves the VPC; for hosted we have options and can adjust retention.
[02:41] Jamie Lawson: Great. What's the onboarding timeline in terms of account provisioning and when we can run the benchmarks?
[02:47] Alex Chen: We can provision a trial account within 48 hours after we get the admin list and region info. Benchmarks — we should schedule them in week 1 of the pilot, target next week if you can get us the traffic patterns and a small sample dataset.
[03:00] Rita Gomez: I'll get the VPC peering details and region preferences by end of week.
[03:05] Alex Chen: Fantastic.
[03:07] Priya Rao: I want to call out a couple of technical notes: 1) KV cache is used for prefixes — if you have long conversation state we can enable prefix caching to reduce token costs; 2) batching settings can be tuned — we'll provide suggested batch sizes and memory profiles; 3) quantization notes — some ops may be slower in certain kernels, we'll include kernel selection guidance.
[03:29] Jamie Lawson: Cool. Is there any required change to our infra for peering? We use strict egress rules.
[03:35] Priya Rao: Usually you need one outbound peering endpoint and a couple firewall rules to allow the control-plane IPs. We'll provide a minimal list.
[03:43] Dr. Isaac Park: On the clinical front we need to ensure model updates are controlled — can you pin model versions?
[03:49] Maya Ortiz: Yes, you can pin to specific model versions and we support canary rollouts with automatic fallback in case of regressions. We also link rollouts to evals so you can gate on quality.
[04:01] Jamie Lawson: Ok, what about monitoring and dashboards? We want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
[04:07] Alex Chen: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, traces, and alerts. We can set up a shared dashboard for Helix and give read-only to auditors.
[04:16] Rita Gomez: For compliance we'll need SOC2/ISO docs. Please send over the certs and any penetration test summaries.
[04:22] Maya Ortiz: Will do — I'll attach the SOC2 report and the security questionnaire answers.
[04:27] Alex Chen: Let's walk through the pilot success criteria quickly. Jamie?
[04:30] Jamie Lawson: Success = p95 latency < 200ms for summarization flows, quality score >= 85% on 1k sample prompts, and no PII leakage in logs.
[04:39] Priya Rao: That sounds reasonable. We'll instrument the benchmarks to produce latency and quality metrics.
[04:44] Jamie Lawson: Any blockers we're seeing?
[04:46] Rita Gomez: Just the paperwork and VPC details. Also need an IP allowlist for the control plane.
[04:53] Alex Chen: We'll include the control plane IP list and the minimal firewall rules in the onboarding doc.
[04:59] Priya Rao: On benchmarks — I'll share a small load test script and a guide for how to produce realistic token distributions; that should help reproduce production-like results.
[05:10] Jamie Lawson: Awesome. Quick question about cost — do you have an estimate for the pilot?
[05:15] Alex Chen: For the pilot footprint you described, if we use dedicated it's about $X/month equivalently — we'll send a pricing estimate. For hosted the variable costs are lower upfront but could be higher at scale. We'll send a pro-forma.
[05:30] Dr. Isaac Park: One more thing — for audit we need immutable logs, is that an option?
[05:35] Maya Ortiz: We can support log export to your S3 and set immutability policies on the bucket, or you can keep logs in your private deployment with retention controls.
[05:44] Jamie Lawson: Great.
[05:45] Alex Chen: Ok, I'll recap: Alex will share onboarding doc + checklist and pricing estimate; Priya will send benchmark script and KMS/KV cache guidance; Maya will send SOC2 and security questionnaire answers; Rita will provide VPC and region details. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next Thursday at the same time.
[06:03] Rita Gomez: That works.
[06:05] Jamie Lawson: Thanks everyone.
[06:07] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
